proposals.title: Snowbally on the floor: one gravity, a body you can pick up, and an edge he peeks back from
proposals.summary: Snowbally now sits on the real floor, the bottom edge of the work area, which on a Mac is the top of the Dock. He looks toward your pointer when it comes near and smiles when you hover over him. When you press him he squashes in the same frame. A quick click still opens the panel with the Springy tap, which now continues from the squash he is already showing. If you hold him or drag more than 4 px, he lifts off the floor with his feet dangling and his shadow stays behind on the floor, shrinking as you carry him higher. Let go and he falls with the same gravity as the launch drop. A short drop ends in a small plop and a long one in the full launch landing with stars and a hello; you can even catch him in mid-air. To get him out of the way, push him against a screen edge and let go, or choose 'Send away' (tray, right-click menu or a global shortcut). He rolls off like a snowball, and only a thin sliver of his body stays at the edge. Because it sits at the screen edge, that sliver is very easy to hit: hover it and he leans in, click it and he rolls home, or drag him out by it. If a question arrives while he is away, he peeks in once with the question mark on the inner side and stays there quietly, the tray shows a small '?', and nothing repeats. Answering gets a warm, equal reaction for Yes and No and a calm one for Later, Not sure or Dismiss. Nothing animates under reduced motion, and you can still move him.
proposals.window:
One BrowserWindow covering exactly the primary display's workArea, a change to window.ts.
- **Current code:** placeBottomRight (window.ts:27-36) gives a 420 px wide window with a 12 px margin.
- **Proposed:** `win.setBounds(screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea)` with no margin. Keep frame:false, transparent, '#00000000', hasShadow:false, alwaysOnTop 'floating', setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces and showInactive.
- **Mission Control:** add `win.setHiddenInMissionControl(true)` so the empty window does not appear there as a giant blank thumbnail.
- **Display changes:** re-apply the bounds on `screen.on('display-metrics-changed' | 'display-added' | 'display-removed')`. This covers the Dock auto-hiding or moving and resolution changes. The renderer needs no new data, because everything is anchored to the window's bottom and right edges (see below).
- **Why a full-area window and not a small window moved with setBounds:** moving a native window from IPC on every pointer event lags the cursor by one or two frames on macOS. Falls, rolls and throws would each need a window move per frame. The panel would also have to be re-measured on every move. Inside one window, everything moves with a compositor transform. R28 already proved this pattern at full height: the work-area height window kept 0.21 % idle CPU and 9–17 ms frames.

**Click-through.** Keep today's pattern (renderer.ts:44-53): `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true,{forward:true})`, switched off while the pointer is over `.rf-avatar` or `.rf-surface`. Three changes:
- (a) **Pin during a drag.** On pointerdown on the avatar, the renderer calls `setIgnore(false)` and `avatarButton.setPointerCapture(pointerId)`. While a drag is in progress, the mousemove handler must not switch back to ignore. Otherwise a fast drag leaves the 64 px box, the window starts ignoring the mouse again and the drag breaks. Unpin on pointerup or pointercancel, then hit-test again.
- (b) **Cheaper hit test.** The window now covers the whole work area, so forwarded mousemove events arrive for the whole screen. Replace `document.elementFromPoint` with a test against two cached rectangles (avatar and surface). Recompute them only when the carrier moves or the panel spring settles. Chromium already delivers mousemove once per frame, so no rAF is needed.
- (c) **One source for hover and gaze.** The same handler computes hover (enter and leave on the avatar rectangle) and the cursor distance used for gaze. Do not rely on synthesized pointerenter events while the window is ignoring the mouse.

**Panel anchoring: the card already rides with him.** In the template, `.rf-avatar` is a child of `.rf-window` (panel.ts:79-147). So `.rf-window` becomes the carrier for both the card and Snowbally.
- **Desktop CSS rule:** `#kt-panel .rf-window { left:0; bottom:0; transform:none }`. JS then writes `style.transform = translate3d(Xpx, -Ypx, 0)` with `X = bodyX - 333` and `Y = 30 + lift`, both rounded to whole device pixels so the pixel art never sits on a fractional offset.
- **Why the constants:** the avatar sits at `right:15px; bottom:-24px` (styles.css:148), the canvas at `left:-12px` and the body centre at canvas x 44. So body centre = card right − 47 and card left = bodyX − 333. With the body's contact row 12 px above the floor, the button bottom is 6 px above the floor and the card bottom is 30 px above it.
- **Frozen values untouched:** card size, springs and the avatar-to-card offset do not change. Every desktop rule gets a `/* desktop (R30): ... */` comment.
- **Making room near an edge:** the card fits only when 345 ≤ bodyX ≤ W − 59 (12 px screen margin on both sides). If he is parked outside that range, opening the panel slides the carrier to the clamped x. The slide uses the panel's own critically damped spring (omega 40) while his body plays `hop`. Because the card rides inside the carrier, it is never detached from him. After the panel closes and its spring settles, he rolls back to his saved spot. The other option, a mirrored card, would change the frozen footer padding `0 90px 0 15px`, so I rejected it.

**Positions.**
- **Saved state:** `{ fromRight: px from the work-area right edge to the body centre, away: null | 'left' | 'right' }` under localStorage `kt-companion.v1`, using the panel's `storage` option. When storage is null (shots) the defaults apply.
- **Default:** fromRight = 79, which is exactly where his body centre is today: work-area right − 12 margin − 20 card inset − 47.
- **Floor:** his contact row is 12 CSS px above the window bottom, so the shadow ends 4 px above the Dock. That is 26 px lower than today, where the contact row is 38 px above the work-area bottom.
- **Load:** clamp to [14, W − 14] (body centre).

**IPC additions (preload.ts).**
- `onCommand(cb)` for main → renderer `kt:command` {away | return | toggle-away | reset-position}.
- `reportState({ away, question })` renderer → main, used for the tray label and title.
- `showContextMenu()` renderer → main, which calls `Menu.popup({ window })`.
- `onPower(cb)` for `powerMonitor` 'resume' and 'unlock-screen'.

**main.ts.**
- **Tray menu:** 'Send Snowbally away' / 'Bring Snowbally back' (with the shortcut shown as the accelerator), 'Put Snowbally back in the corner' (reset position), 'Reset demo', 'Hide completely' (today's win.hide, labelled as stopping questions), 'Quit'.
- **Tray click:** toggles away and back instead of hide and show.
- **Pending question while away:** `tray.setTitle(' ?')` and the tooltip 'Snowbally has a question'.
- **Global shortcut:** `globalShortcut.register('CommandOrControl+Alt+Shift+S', toggleAway)` (proposed default). If `register` returns false, log it and leave the accelerator off the tray item. Call `globalShortcut.unregisterAll()` on 'will-quit'.
- **second-instance** already shows the window; it now also sends `return`.

**Optional, behind a flag:** `win.setFocusable(false)` while the panel is closed and `setFocusable(true)` + `focus()` on open. Clicking or dragging him would then no longer pull focus away from the engineer's terminal. It needs checking on macOS; it is off by default.
proposals.drag:
**State machine** (new `companion.ts`): grounded → pressed → (click | held | carried) → airborne → landing → grounded. A separate branch handles away.

**pointerdown on .rf-avatar.**
- Draws the press pose synchronously, so it shows on the next paint. The pose is `click` frame 1 (crouch, happy), so no new pose is needed.
- Keeps the frozen `motion.press(true)` 2 px canvas dip (panel-motion.ts:110, 248).
- Pins the window to receive the mouse and captures the pointer.
- Interrupts any act, including the airborne fall: pressing on a falling Snowbally catches him.

**Click.** Released within 350 ms and less than 4 px from the press point: toggle the panel and play `click` from frame 2 (deep squash). The Springy tap continues from the squash he is already showing instead of repeating frames 0–1. This needs `run(act, from)`, which already exists (avatar.ts:314).

**Double-click.** A second release within 300 ms and less than 4 px from the first does not toggle again; the panel keeps whatever the first click did. It plays `backflip` on the uncropped drop surface.

**Hold, HOLD_LIFT_MS = 350.** Holding still for 350 ms lifts him: the carried pose and a 4 px lift. This tells the user he can be moved without them reading anything. Releasing then sets him down with the small plop and does not toggle the panel.

**Drag threshold.** When the pointer moves 4 px or more (the brief's value), call `motion.press(false)`. If the panel is open, close it with the frozen close spring, which shrinks the card into him. Then switch to the carried pose and lift him 4 px. Set `cursor:grabbing` on the stage (desktop CSS addition); the button keeps its frozen `cursor:pointer`.

**Carried pose** (composed only from orb() parameters, matching `backflip` frame 5): `{ shape: 'stretch', feet: [{side:-1}, {side:1}], expression: 'surprised' }` for 120 ms, then `'happy'`.
- Gaze follows the drag direction when |vx| > 300 px/s (−1 or +1), otherwise 0.
- The expression returns to 'surprised' while |v| > 1500 px/s.
- The scene shadow is not drawn while he is carried. A new floor-shadow canvas (`.rf-shadow`, a stage-level sibling of `.rf-window`, 44×7 source px, `pointer-events:none`) stays on the floor at his x. It uses `kit.shadow` with width 26 when height < 16 px, 22 below 64, 18 below 192 and 14 above that, and is redrawn only when the width tier changes.
- This is the R28 idea of a shadow waiting on the floor, which R28 could do with the static display canvas. Here the display canvas moves with him, so the shadow needs its own canvas.

**Following the pointer.**
- The carrier follows the pointer 1:1 at the grab offset: one transform write per rAF while the drag lasts, with no spring lag because direct manipulation must feel attached.
- The body centre is clamped to x ∈ [−14, W + 14] and y between the floor and the work-area top.
- He can go half past a side edge, but the pointer stops at the screen edge.

**Pushing past an edge.**
- When the pointer is within 2 px of the left or right screen edge and the body centre is within 6 px of that edge (about half his body outside), he shows a telegraph: front view, gaze toward the edge, 'happy'.
- Releasing there means leave: he slides out at max(600 px/s, release speed) into the tucked position.
- Releasing anywhere else on screen keeps him fully on screen.

**Throw velocity.** Use the pointer samples from the last 80 ms. Speeds under 250 px/s count as 0, so a normal drop never flings him. Clamp |vx| and |vy| to 1400 px/s. A throw toward a wall never leaves the screen: on contact with the wall, vx is set to 0 and he falls straight down. Leaving only happens through the deliberate push past an edge.

**Release in the air.**
- **One gravity.** The brief says to reuse R28's fall: a 900 ms constant-acceleration drop from the top of a work area about 900 px tall works out to about 2200 px/s² (2·900/0.81² ≈ 2222). Make that one constant: G = 2200 px/s² in `physics.ts`.
- **Change to R28:** the launch fall time becomes sqrt(2h/G), which is still about 0.9 s on a 13-inch MacBook, so launch and release share one physics.
- **Ballistic motion:** x += vx·dt, vy += G·dt, y += vy·dt. The ceiling (top of the work area) sets vy to 0.
- **Surfaces:** while airborne, the falling pose (R28 `renderFalling`, stretch with air streaks) is drawn on the drop canvas. That canvas is a child of the button, so it moves with the carrier and the streaks are not cropped.
- **Catchable mid-air:** the hitbox moves with the body, so you can grab him while he falls.

**Landing: three tiers by impact speed v.**
- **Small, v < 300 px/s** (about a 20 px drop): composed settle, `{shape:'crouch'}` for 62 ms then `{shape:'low'}` for 62 ms, then rest.
- **Medium, v < 900 px/s** (up to about 180 px): `entrance` frames 5–11 on the drop surface (impact pancake, spring back, settle), 0.44 s. This needs a new `to` bound on run().
- **Large:** `entrance` frames 5–23, the full R28 landing with stars and hello, 1.19 s.
- **Snow sticks:** horizontal velocity is set to 0 at touchdown, so there is no sliding.

**After landing.** Save `fromRight`, play the shadow-to-scene handover (hide `.rf-shadow` because the entrance frames draw their own shadow), then return to the base mode (idle, or the processing loop if `busy`).

**Reduced motion.** Dragging still follows the pointer 1:1, because that is user-driven manipulation. The carried and press poses are still frames. Release places him on the floor immediately (one landing frame `entrance` 20, then rest). There is no throw velocity, no fall and no roll. A push past an edge tucks him away immediately.

**Edge cases.**
- **pointercancel or window blur mid-drag:** treat it as a release at the last position.
- **Drag started while away:** pulls him out, and landing makes that the new spot.
- **Drag while processing:** physics owns the body, and the loop resumes after landing.
- **Panel open at drag start:** it closes and does not reopen by itself.
- **Display metrics change mid-drag:** end the drag and land.
- **Keyboard:** while the avatar button has focus, ←/→ roll him 22 px (one turn step), and Shift+←/→ send him away to that edge, so moving is not mouse-only.
proposals.leaveReturn:
**Ways to leave** (all equal):
- (1) Push him against the left or right screen edge while dragging and release (see Drag).
- (2) Right-click Snowbally to get a native context menu via `Menu.popup`: 'Send away', 'Open panel', 'Put back in the corner'. While the menu is open he holds `peek` frame 4 (quarter view, attentive), then rests.
- (3) Tray 'Send Snowbally away', or a tray click.
- (4) The global shortcut (proposed CommandOrControl+Alt+Shift+S, a toggle).
- (5) Shift+←/→ while he has focus.

If the panel is open, its frozen close spring starts at the same moment. The card is inside the carrier, so it shrinks into him as he starts moving.

**How he leaves: a snowball roll, from parameters only.**
- He rolls to the nearest side edge using `orb({ turn })` with the authored TURN_POSES 1..7 (minimal-kit.ts:32-41) and the body shape 'neutral'.
- **No slipping:** one turn step per 22 CSS px travelled. His circumference is π·28 source px ≈ 176 CSS px, divided by 8 face positions.
- **Speed:** acceleration 1600 px/s², top speed 900 px/s, and an ease-in to the tucked position over the last 40 px.
- **Duration:** from the default spot (about 60 px from the right edge) the roll takes about 0.35 s; from mid-screen about 1.1 s.
- **Rolling left** uses the sequence 7→1. The direction must be checked on a rendered strip and the sequence swapped if the face appears to turn the wrong way.
- The floor shadow travels with him.

**What stays visible: the 'tab' is him.** No new tab art is drawn.
- **Tucked position:** the body centre is 18 CSS px beyond the edge, so 5 source columns (10 CSS px) of his outline and white body, plus a bit of shadow, stay on screen. The window boundary clips the rest.
- **Hit area:** the visible part of the 64 px button is 14×64 px. Because the pointer stops at the screen edge, that strip is effectively infinitely wide in the direction of travel, so it is very easy to hit (Fitts's law). This does not hold if the Dock sits on that side; see the risks.
- **Still:** the idle timer stops while he is tucked (a still frame, zero timers).
- **Accessibility:** the aria-label becomes 'Snowbally, away at the right edge. Press to bring him back'.

**Hover on the sliver.** He leans in 8 px (a 150 ms rAF spring on the carrier), with gaze toward the pointer and 'happy'. When the pointer leaves he slides back out. This is how a person who has never read anything finds out the sliver is him.

**Ways back:**
- (1) Click the sliver. He rolls back to his saved spot using the same kinematics, then plays `hello` once.
- (2) Drag him out by the sliver. He is carried, and wherever he lands becomes his new spot.
- (3) Tray 'Bring Snowbally back', or a tray click.
- (4) The global shortcut.
- (5) Launching the app again (the second-instance handler sends `return`).
- (6) Anything that opens the panel programmatically. showError (panel.ts:587-599) and `?open=1` call `companion.ensureOnScreen()` first, so the card never opens next to an off-screen avatar.

(1) and (2) need no reading at all.

**A question arrives while he is away.**
- **Today's code:** the collapsed panel never polls (`syncPoll` runs only while the panel is open, panel.ts:517-520), and the glyph shows only while the question view is open (`hasQuestion = panelOpen && view==='question'`, panel.ts:205).
- **New `question-watch.ts`:** while the panel is closed (on screen or away), poll `api.questions` every 60 s with one setInterval. Skip the poll if there is no identity or the window is busy. Also refresh immediately on `kt:show`, on powerMonitor 'resume' and 'unlock-screen', and on return. A question counts as new when its id has not been seen (seen ids are kept in memory and in storage).
- **Peek-in:** a 2-step roll (300 ms) from tucked to peeking, with the body centre 20 CSS px inside the edge so his face is fully visible. Then he plays the authored `question` act once (1.33 s: glance, rise, glyph) and holds a still rest frame with the glyph.
- **Glyph on the inner side:** the glyph sprite is drawn on the inward side. That is the authored x 64 at the left edge, and the mirrored x 27 at the right edge (48 − 16 − 5), still inside the crop (x ≥ 26). The glyph is repositioned, not redrawn.
- **Tray:** title set to ' ?'.
- **No repeats:** the same question never makes him peek again. A second question while he is already peeking only updates the panel count.
- **Clicking him while peeking:** he rolls home and the panel opens on that question's view, a quiet programmatic open with no extra act because `question` already played.
- **Question answered or expired elsewhere:** he slides back to the tucked position and the tray title is cleared.
- **Reduced motion:** he jumps straight to the peeking position as a still frame with the glyph.

**Launch while away.** He starts tucked, with no launch fall, respecting where the user sent him. This is an open question for Artem.
proposals.reactions:
**Priority rules:**
- **P0 physics** (pressed, held, carried, airborne, landing, rolling, peeking in) owns the body. Acts cannot interrupt it. One P2 act waits in a queue (newest wins) and plays after the physics ends.
- **P1 direct input** (press, click tap, double-click, right-click, file drag) interrupts any P2 or P3 act immediately. This is the lab rule: the engineer's action beats a flourish.
- **P2 product events** interrupt P3. If a P1 act is playing, they wait until it ends, except `error`, which plays immediately.
- **P3 ambient** (fidget, welcome-back hello, gaze, hover face) is dropped, not queued, if anything else is playing.
- **Return after a one-shot:** every one-shot returns to the base mode. That is the `processing` loop while `busy` and `idle3` otherwise. Today `play('click')` during processing kills the loop for good, because play() calls stop() and then rest() (avatar.ts:302-311, 332).
- **Uncropped surface for tall acts:** `hop` (lowest bottom 64 puts the top at row 36, below the crop's top row 42), `backflip` (top row 24), `half` (top row 36) and `hero` are routed to the drop canvas. This generalises R28's surface. Today these acts would be cropped, but the panel never plays them.

**Pointer:**
- **Hover enter** (from the renderer's cached hit test): same frame, the current idle pose with gaze toward the pointer. After 250 ms of dwell, 'happy' face (one draw). On leave, back to the idle loop. This changes the brief's hover = `peek`: peek turns his face away to the right (gaze +1, quarter view) for a second, which reads as ignoring you.
- **Pointer within 160 px of his body centre** (on screen, no act playing):
  - gaze −1 when dx < −20 px, +1 when dx > 20 px, otherwise 0, with 6 px of hysteresis;
  - drawn once per change, through a new `avatar.look(gaze)` that redraws the current idle pose;
  - gaze goes back to 0 600 ms after the pointer leaves the radius;
  - when the panel is open and the pointer is over the card, gaze is −1, so he looks at the question with you.
- **Gaze only, no quarter view:** the kit's quarter view only shifts the face to the right (`faceX + 2`, minimal-kit.ts:114), so it cannot track a pointer on the left.
- **Idle renderer with gaze:** `renderIdlePose(kit, target, pose, gaze)` reproduces idle3 exactly at gaze 0 (clear, then shadow width 26, then `orb({shape})`), checked by a parity test.

**Press, release and moves:**
- **pointerdown:** `click` frame 1, plus the frozen 2 px press dip, in the same frame.
- **Click:** toggle the panel, then `click` from frame 2 (0.53 s).
- **Double-click:** `backflip`, 1.5 s, uncropped.
- **Hold 350 ms:** carried pose with a 4 px lift.
- **Drag:** carried pose, with gaze and expression following speed.
- **Release:** a landing tier (small 0.12 s / medium 0.44 s / large 1.19 s).
- **Right-click:** `peek` frame 4 held while the menu is open.
- **Files dragged over him:** `input` (surprised, 0.67 s), then the existing drop handler opens the input view.

**Panel and product:**
- **Question arrives, panel closed, on screen:** the `question` act once (1.33 s), then idle with the static glyph. This changes the brief's `hop`: the lab table asks for 'one small pose change, then a static available cue', and `question` is the authored act for that moment.
- **Question arrives, panel open on another view:** count badge only, so their work is not interrupted.
- **Question arrives while away:** peek in (see Leave/return).
- **Opening the question view:** `question` (unchanged).
- **Yes and No:** `hop`, 1.125 s, uncropped, identical for both, replacing today's `result`. Correction is welcomed as much as confirmation. This changes the brief's `hello`: answering is the moment that matters most, and hop is the warmer of the two.
- **Not sure:** `hello`, 0.67 s. This replaces the brief's `stretching`, whose yawn (frames 6–11, expression 'yawn') reads as boredom.
- **Later:** `peek`, 1.0 s. Accepted; it ends 'happy' and 'available'.
- **Dismiss:** the composed 'low' settle, 2 frames (125 ms). This rejects the brief's `half`: its sheepish beat suggests he has been let down, which the lab rules forbid.
- **Undo:** `peek`.
- **Points burst:** unchanged; it rides on the hop.
- **Investigation:** `processing` loop and then `result` (unchanged).
- **Failure:** `error` (unchanged).
- **Retry succeeded:** `hello` (unchanged).
- **Return from away:** `hello` once on arrival, or `question` if one is pending.
- **Launch:** R28, landing at his saved x.
- **Make-room slide:** `hop`.
- **Welcome back:** after powerMonitor 'unlock-screen' or 'resume', following at least 20 min without any interaction, he plays `hello` once when the pointer first comes within 160 px. He greets you when you come near, not when the lid opens.
- **Idle fidget** (P3), changed from 'every 45–90 s':
  - eligible only after 3 min without interaction, with the panel closed, on screen, no glyph showing and the pointer more than 160 px away;
  - never within 2 min of launch;
  - at most 1 per 4 min and 8 per hour;
  - chosen by weight: `peek` 3, `stretching` 2, `hop` 1;
  - one setTimeout, re-armed on any interaction;
  - if he is sent away within 15 s of a fidget twice in a day, fidgets stop for that day.

**Reduced motion** (`canAnimate()` false):
- No acts, no fidgets, no gaze tracking and no hover face.
- Direct manipulation still works: the press and carried poses are still frames, and the carrier follows the pointer.
- Release, leave, return and peek-in jump straight to their end state, each showing that act's `stillFrame`.
- The glyph is still shown.
- No sound anywhere.
risks: Full-work-area transparent always-on-top window: compositing and present bandwidth while he moves may exceed the 20 ms frame budget on lower-end Macs; measure first (plan B in the performance section).

Electron's forwarded mousemove (setIgnoreMouseEvents forward:true) can miss events on fast approaches. A missed event at pointerdown would let the click pass through to the app underneath; pinning the window to receive the mouse on pointerdown, plus pointer capture, only helps once the event has arrived.
Click versus drag on trackpads: tap jitter or a slow tap-and-hold may be read as a drag or a lift (4 px and 350 ms need tuning with real users).
A double-click now plays a backflip without closing the panel; users who habitually double-click may be surprised.
The TURN_POSES order for rolling left versus right is unverified; the roll may read as spinning backwards until a strip is checked.
Fitts's-law edge targets fail if the Dock sits on the left or right, because the work-area edge is then not the screen edge. The sliver stays clickable but loses the edge advantage.
Polling questions while the panel is collapsed is new background work: the 60 s interval must stay inside the 0.3 % idle budget, and the service must tolerate it.
Clicking or dragging Snowbally activates the app and takes focus from the engineer's current app; setFocusable(false) while collapsed might fix this but is not yet checked on macOS.
Moving the glyph to the left side and repositioning the floor shadow are layout changes to authored elements; the lab or Artem may treat that as touching frozen art.
Lowering him 26 px to the true floor and moving the panel with him changes the screenshot baselines and the hitbox invariant the harness checks today; the checks must be redefined, not loosened.
A saved position can become invalid after display changes (clamped on load, but a remembered away side with a newly added side Dock may look odd).

Cursor awareness could read as surveillance; it only uses distance and direction within 160 px, stores nothing, and works only within his own window, in line with the lab's warning about implying he sees other apps.

proposals.title: Snowbally UX pass: "asks once, thanks warmly, remembers his place" (participation-and-warmth proposal)
proposals.summary: Snowbally sits wherever you put him along the bottom of the screen. He perks up when your cursor comes near. When you press him he squashes, and when you drag him he dangles from the cursor. If you let go in the air he falls with the same gravity as the launch drop and lands with a plop. If he is in your way, you flick him off either edge: he rolls out of sight and leaves a thin white sliver of his body at the edge. Clicking the sliver, the tray, the context menu or a shortcut brings him back to the same spot, and he says "hello again". When someone needs your knowledge he hops once and shows a small question mark. If you are not at your desk, he saves the hop for when you come back. If he is tucked away at the edge, he peeks in with his face and the question mark. One click on him opens that question with Yes already focused. Yes and No get the same warm wave. Not sure, Later and Dismiss get a friendly nod, never a sad face. He never asks twice: one hop when a question arrives and at most one quiet glance on a later return. If he came out of hiding to ask, he goes back to his corner after you answer. Otherwise he stays still apart from the existing three-pose breathing and an occasional stretch during long quiet stretches.
proposals.window:
DECISION: one frameless, transparent, always-on-top window covering the whole primary work area. The current 420 px panel becomes a "dock" box that moves inside it. I accept the brief's full-work-area idea and keep a fallback flag.

What the code does today, as read: window.ts sets the window to 420 x max(680, workArea.height - 12) at the right edge with a 12 px margin. It calls setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, {forward:true}). renderer.ts toggles that on every mousemove through elementFromPoint(...).closest('.rf-avatar, .rf-surface'). #kt-panel is position:fixed; inset:0. .rf-window sits bottom:44px, is centred and 380 px wide (so left = 20 px in a 420 px window). The .rf-avatar 64 px hitbox sits right:15px; bottom:-24px inside it, which puts the hitbox centre 353 px from the dock's left edge and its bottom 20 px above the dock's bottom.

New shell (window.ts, desktop-only):
- placeWorkArea(win) replaces placeBottomRight and calls win.setBounds(screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea) exactly.
- createCompanionWindow keeps frame:false, transparent, hasShadow:false, alwaysOnTop 'floating', setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces and click-through by default.
- main.ts listens to screen 'display-metrics-changed', 'display-added' and 'display-removed'. On any of them it calls setBounds again and sends 'kt:area' {width, height}. The renderer re-clamps Snowbally's position, with no animation.

Renderer layout:
- A new wrapper <div class="kt-dock"> (420 x 680 CSS px, the existing WINDOW.height) holds #kt-panel. #kt-panel changes from position:fixed; inset:0 to position:absolute; inset:0 inside the dock, marked "desktop (R30)".
- The dock moves only by transform: translate3d(dockX, 0, 0). Its bottom is pinned 12 px above the work-area bottom, so the floor (hitbox bottom) stays exactly where it is today, 32 px above the work-area bottom.
- Position is stored as the body centre's distance from the right edge (fromRight). The default is 12 + (420 - 353) = 79 px, so the first launch looks identical to R28.
- dockX = (W - fromRight) - 353.
- If dockX < 8 (the card would leave the screen on the left), the dock switches to data-side="left". This is a desktop-only mirror: .rf-avatar uses left:15px; right:auto, the .rf-footer padding becomes 0 15px 0 90px, and dockX = bodyX - 67. The side is chosen only when the panel opens or a drag ends, never mid-drag, so the card never jumps under the person.
- All frozen v008/v009 values (type, spacing, colours, springs) stay as they are.

Hit-testing:
- elementFromPoint is replaced by arithmetic against cached rects (body hitbox, open .rf-surface, the away tab). They are refreshed on dock move end, panel spring settle and 'kt:area'.
- The mousemove handler is O(1) and returns early when the pointer is more than 200 px from every rect.
- While a drag is in progress the renderer pins setIgnore(false) until pointerup or pointercancel, so a fast drag can never release the window and send the mouseup to the app underneath. On macOS, mouseDragged events stay with the window where the press began, even over the Dock.
- document mouseleave and window blur force ignore=true, as today.

Why one big window instead of moving a 420 px window with win.setPosition during drag:
- Dragging becomes a compositor transform in the same frame as the pointer event. There is no IPC round trip and no one-frame lag of the native window behind the cursor.
- The R28 fall, the roll off the edge and the peek-in all happen inside one surface.
- The panel can open beside him anywhere along the floor.

Fallback: a KT_WINDOW_MODE=column flag keeps today's 420 px window and moves it with win.setPosition from 'kt:move' IPC messages carrying screenX. I recommend it only if the harness memory or CPU budgets below fail.
proposals.drag:
Drag state machine (new src/apps/desktop/place.ts), driven by pointer events on .rf-avatar:

1. pointerdown (P0):
   - In the same handler, synchronously draw the composed pose PRESS: orb {shape:'crouch', expression:'normal'}. The existing motion.press(true) 2 px translateY stays.
   - Any act playing is interrupted, including fidgets and an arrival hop. Touching him counts as having seen the arrival.
   - Call setPointerCapture, record the start point, the grab offset and t0, and pin click-through off.
2. Click or drag: the pointer becomes a drag once it has moved more than 4 px (Euclidean distance) from the start. I accept the brief's 4 px. Trackpad tap jitter is absorbed by one extra rule: if the release comes within 180 ms with less than 8 px of movement, it still counts as a click.
   - On a click, the existing root click handler runs (toggle plus avatar.play('click'), 0.67 s).
   - After a real drag, a capture-phase click listener calls stopPropagation once (suppressNextClick), so dropping him never toggles the panel.
3. Drag start:
   - If the panel is open, close it with the existing spring (closePanel) and remember wasOpen.
   - Set the CSS cursor to grabbing.
   - Draw the carried pose, depending on height above the floor h = floorY - (pointerY + grabOffsetY):
     - h <= 12 px: SCOOT on the display canvas: orb {shape:'low', feet:[{side:-1},{side:1}], gaze: dir}. He slides along the floor.
     - h > 12 px: HELD: orb {shape:'stretch', expression: 'surprised' for the first 150 ms, then 'happy', feet:[{side:-1},{side:1}] as dangling contact nubs, gaze: dir}. The body is drawn on the existing .rf-drop surface (the R28 mechanism) and lifted with translateY(-h). The display canvas shows renderFloorShadow(), so his shadow stays on the floor under him.
   - dir = sign(vx) when |vx| > 0.25 px/ms (velocity averaged over the last 80 ms), otherwise 0. view:'quarter' is used only when moving right at more than 0.6 px/ms, because the kit's quarter view always shifts the face +2 px to the right (drawFace: faceX = x + 2). There is no left-facing quarter, and I do not mirror the art.
   - The pose is redrawn only when its key (shape|expression|gaze|view) changes, typically 2 to 6 draws per drag. Position is a transform on the dock (x) and on .rf-drop (y) on every pointermove.
   - Clamps: body centre x in [44, W - 44] while held, except during an off-edge gesture (see below). y between 0 and the floor.
4. Release on the floor (h <= 12): redraw idle, no fall.
5. Release in the air: a fall with constant acceleration using the same gravity as the launch drop.
   - G = 2·|fallStart| / 0.9², computed at runtime from AvatarController.fallStart(), so a release from the top of the screen takes exactly ENTRANCE_FALL_MS. Example: 200 px on a 1,000 px work area takes about 0.38 s.
   - t = sqrt(2h / G). The body uses renderFalling() (stretch plus the two air streaks, toggled every 62.5 ms), and the shadow waits on the floor.
   - Landing:
     - h < 160 px: a plop, hop frames 11 to 17 ('Land', 'deep' to 'Hello again', 7 frames at 16 fps ≈ 0.44 s).
     - h >= 160 px: the authored entrance from ENTRANCE_IMPACT_FRAME 5 (impact, spring back, stars, hello; 19 frames ≈ 1.19 s), exactly as R28.
6. Off-edge release means leave (see leaveReturn). It triggers when the body centre is within 16 px of either edge at release, or on a fling: |vx| >= 1.5 px/ms toward the nearer edge with the body within 160 px of it.
7. After landing:
   - Persist {fromRight, side} to the panel's storage under 'kt-desktop.place.v1'.
   - Set data-side from the new x.
   - If wasOpen, call openPanel() programmatically (quiet, as v009 intends for non-click opens), so his conversation follows him.
8. Edge cases:
   - pointercancel or blur mid-drag: treat as a release at the current point.
   - A display change mid-drag: finish the drag, then clamp.
   - A persisted position outside the current area is clamped on load.
   - A launch with a stored position falls in at that x.
   - Keyboard: with .rf-avatar focused, Option+Left/Right moves him 48 px with one SCOOT frame. Option+Down sends him away to the nearer edge.
   - Reduced motion: dragging still follows the pointer, because direct manipulation is not animation. PRESS, SCOOT and HELD are single static frames. A release in the air puts him on the floor instantly with idle drawn; no fall and no landing act.
9. New Avatar API needed:
   - hold(spec: OrbSpec, surface: 'display' | 'drop', liftPx)
   - fallFrom(liftPx, then: {act, from})
   - playFrom(act, frame)
   - status().held / .liftPx

Harness: dispatch synthetic pointer sequences with webContents.sendInputEvent (mouseDown / mouseMove x 30 / mouseUp). Assert the pose change on the first pointermove past 4 px, no panel toggle after a drag, a landing within t ± 1 frame, and drag frames with max ≤ 20 ms.
proposals.leaveReturn:
Two separate meanings, named plainly in the tray:
- "Step aside" (away): he leaves the screen but questions still reach you.
- "Hide completely": today's win.hide(). Nothing reaches you; this is Do Not Disturb.
Today the tray has only Show/Hide, and the panel stops polling when hidden because document.hidden is checked in the poll.

LEAVE (from an off-edge drag or fling, Option+Down, the context-menu item "Step aside", the tray item "Step aside", or the global shortcut):
1. Close the panel if it is open.
2. Glance toward the edge for 190 ms (3 frames at 16 fps): front view with gaze ±1, plus view:'quarter' only for the right edge.
3. ROLL: orb {shape:'tuck', bottom:80} with turn stepping 1→7 for rightward travel and 7→1 for leftward at 16 fps. These are the backflip's own TURN_POSES, read in minimal-kit.ts; no new art. The dock translates with ease-in to edge + 60 px, taking clamp(distance / 1.4 px/ms, 280, 700) ms. This is the only rAF and it stops when the roll ends.
4. Once he is off-window, the display canvas leaves the viewport. AvatarController's IntersectionObserver then calls rest() and stops the idle setTimeout, so nothing ticks while he is away.

What remains visible is the SLIVER: a new 24 x 64 CSS px element <canvas class="kt-tab"> flush with the edge at floor level. It is drawn once per state change with the kit through a new avatar.renderInto(canvas, spec, cropX). It shows his idle body at a horizontal offset so that only 6 source px (12 CSS px) of his rim are visible: contour, white fill and base shade. That is the edge of the body without the face, so there is no eye looking at you all day. No new anatomy.
- Hover over the sliver (P1, static): he leans out to 10 source px, enough to show one cheek, as one redraw. The cursor is pointer and the aria-label is "Bring Snowbally back".
- The tab is part of the interactive hit-test rects.
- Reduced motion: leaving is instant and the sliver appears directly.

RETURN, five ways:
1. Click the sliver. This is the discoverable way: a white piece of him at the edge reads as "he is behind there".
2. Drag the sliver: you pull him out and place him anywhere, through the normal drag state machine.
3. Tray: the menu item toggles between "Step aside" and "Bring Snowbally back". A tray click while he is away brings him back instead of hiding the window.
4. Global shortcut: globalShortcut.register('Control+Option+K'), proposed. If registration returns false it is logged and the item is simply not shown, and the key is listed as an open question. Avoid Control+Option+Space: it is macOS's default input-source switcher.
5. app 'second-instance' (launching the app again) brings him back.

Return animation:
- ROLL in from the edge to the remembered fromRight, ease-out, clamp(distance / 1.2 px/ms, 300, 900) ms.
- Then hop frames 11 to 17. The authored beat at frame 14 is literally named "Hello again".
- Reduced motion: he appears in place.

A QUESTION ARRIVES WHILE AWAY:
- Polling continues while away (see engagement).
- The sliver slides out over 160 ms to 14 source px (28 CSS px), enough to show his face. It then plays PEEK-IN, a 12 fps composition that mirrors the authored 'question' act using kit parameters only:
  - f0-2: neutral, gaze 0
  - f3-5: 'high', gaze toward the screen (-1 at the right edge, +1 at the left edge)
  - f6 onward: neutral, same gaze
  - The question glyph, extracted from the accepted art as today, appears from f3.
- At the right edge the glyph is drawn at bodyLeft - 7 instead of its authored scene x 64. At x 64 it sits on his right side, which would be off-screen. Only the glyph's position changes, never its pixels. At the left edge the authored position is already on the visible side.
- He then holds that still frame with the glyph. It is static: no timer, no repetition.
- Clicking the peeking face brings him back (roll in, plus "Hello again") and opens the panel directly on that question with Yes focused (the existing focusFor('question')).
- Because he only came out to ask, a returnToAway flag is set. When the panel next closes (after an answer, or with Escape), he waits 1.2 s and rolls back to the same edge, unless you dragged him in the meantime. Your earlier "you are in my way" is respected.
- Reduced motion: the sliver widens to the face-plus-glyph frame instantly.
- On macOS the tray also shows Tray.setTitle('?') while a question is waiting, whether or not he is away. That is my proposal; it is listed as an open question.

At launch with away persisted ('kt-desktop.place.v1'.away = 'left' or 'right'): there is no fall. The sliver does one 1 s peek-in without the glyph (unless a question is waiting), then shrinks back, so a relaunch is never mistaken for a crash.

Context menu: right-click on Snowbally sends 'kt:context-menu'. Main calls Menu.popup with:
- "Step aside"
- "Open questions (n)"
- "Little idle moves ✓"
- "Reset position"
- "Settings…"
This is the discoverable way to send him away for people who do not think of dragging him off.
proposals.reactions:
PRIORITY LEVELS (new src/libs/utils/motion/director.ts wraps avatar.play):
- P0, direct manipulation: press, drag, release, fall, landing.
- P1, caused by the person: click; input, processing, result and error (existing calls); answer reactions; leave and return rolls; undo.
- P2, ambient announcements: question arrival, the return greeting, the single reminder.
- P3, fidgets.

Rules:
- A higher level interrupts a lower one immediately.
- At the same level the newer act replaces the older, except that the processing loop is replaced only by result, error or P0.
- P2 never interrupts P1 and never plays while the panel is open, a drag is active or the person is typing. It waits in a one-slot queue for up to 10 s after the last P1 act ends. If it still cannot play, the announcement is kept as "unannounced" and retried at the next eligible moment (subject to frequency rules); it is not dropped.
- P3 is discarded whenever anything else is pending.
- Every act passes through AvatarController.canAnimate(), which already turns play() into rest() under reduced motion, a hidden document or an off-screen canvas.

EVENT → RESPONSE (durations from the fps and frames read in core-acts.ts and state-acts.ts):
- Pointer enters the body, idle and not dragging: PERK, a static orb {shape:'high', gaze: side of the pointer}, one draw. Pointer leaves: back to the idle pose. REJECTED: the brief's "hover = peek". A 1.0 s act on every pass of the cursor near the screen corner is noise, and peek is reserved for the reminder below.
- Cursor within 160 px of the body centre (from forwarded mousemove): the idle poses are drawn with gaze = sign(dx) when |dx| > 24 px, plus view:'quarter' only when the pointer is to the right and |dx| > 64. One draw per change of gaze. Gaze returns to 0 600 ms after the pointer leaves the radius. Requires a new idle-with-look render: the idle3 shapes neutral/low/high plus gaze/view, composed from kit parameters. Off under reduced motion, while away and while an act plays.
- pointerdown: PRESS (crouch), static, P0.
- Click (release without a drag): 'click' Springy tap, 10 frames at 15 fps = 0.67 s, P1, plus the existing toggle. If the glyph is showing, the panel opens directly on the newest pending question rather than the restored view. That is a two-click path from noticing to answering.
- Drag start, carry, release, fall, landing: see the drag section (SCOOT, HELD, renderFalling, hop[11..17] at 0.44 s, entrance[5..23] at 1.19 s).
- Fling or drop off an edge: glance plus ROLL (0.47 to 0.89 s), then the sliver.
- Brought back: ROLL in, then hop[11..17] ("Hello again").
- Typing the first character, pasting or attaching: 'input' (0.67 s), unchanged.
- Send: 'processing' loop, then 'result' (0.8 s) or 'error' (0.83 s), unchanged.
- Question arrival while collapsed and the person is present (P2): 'hop' (18 frames at 16 fps = 1.125 s), then 'question' (16 frames at 12 fps = 1.33 s), then rest with the glyph overlay. The glyph is static on the idle poses, so it costs no extra draws. I accept "hop + glyph", and hop becomes reserved for "something for you" and "hello again", which is why it is removed from the fidget pool.
- Question arrival while the panel is open, while processing or while typing: no motion. The .rf-count badge and the glyph update silently.
- Question arrival while away: PEEK-IN (described above).
- Yes or No: 'hello' (10 frames at 15 fps = 0.67 s) for both, equally warm (the lab's rule); the receipt shows the recorded answer. Changes respond(), which today plays 'result' for every value. If the answer empties the queue and it is the first time today: 'backflip' (1.5 s) instead of hello, the "all caught up" moment. Behind a flag.
- Not sure, Later, Dismiss: NOD, a new composition: 8 frames at 15 fps = 0.53 s.
  - f0-1: low, blink
  - f2-4: neutral, normal
  - f5-7: neutral, happy
  REJECTED from the brief:
  - Dismiss = 'half': its 'sheepish' face and almost-flip read as embarrassment, and the lab brief says Unknown, Later and Dismiss get "a neutral friendly settle, with no disappointment".
  - Not sure = 'stretching': a yawn after "not sure" reads as boredom.
  - Later = 'peek': kept for the reminder.
- Undo: 'peek' (16 frames at 16 fps = 1.0 s), meaning "okay, back to it".
- Points enabled: the existing pixel burst in the receipt plus the same hello. Unchanged.
- Service reconnected or Reset demo: 'hello', unchanged.
- Return after being away from the desk (P2, after 'unlock-screen' or 'resume' with at least 20 min away, played 1.2 s after the event). The first matching rule wins:
  1. An unannounced question is waiting: the arrival sequence.
  2. An announced but never-opened question is waiting and not yet reminded: one 'peek' (1.0 s), the only reminder that question ever gets.
  3. First return of the local day: 'stretching' (20 frames at 16 fps = 1.25 s), "good morning".
  4. At least 2 h since the last greeting: 'hello'.
  5. Otherwise nothing.
- Fidget (P3): 'stretching' or 'peek', alternating and never the same act twice in a row; rules under engagement. REJECTED: 'hop' as a fidget.
- Double-click = 'backflip': REJECTED. Detecting a double-click means delaying the single click by about 250 ms, which breaks "answers within one frame" and conflicts with the v009 toggle plus Springy tap. backflip moves to "all caught up".
- Props ('moonwalk', 'hero'): not used in this pass (open question).

REDUCED MOTION (system preference or the existing reducedMotion setting): no act plays (the existing gate). PRESS, SCOOT and HELD are shown as single static frames because they are direct feedback. No cursor gaze or perk. Falls, rolls, peek-in and landings are instant. Arrival shows only the glyph and the tray '?'. No fidgets. No sound anywhere.
proposals.engagement:
THE GAP TODAY, from panel.ts: syncPoll() only runs while state.panelOpen ("no timer at all while collapsed"), and hasQuestion() is `state.panelOpen && state.view === 'question'`. So a question that arrives while Snowbally is collapsed, which is most of the day, is invisible until the person happens to open the panel. The glyph on the idle body never shows when it would matter. Fixing this is the biggest participation gain in the pass.

1. Arrival reaches the person:
   - A background check of api.questions() runs every 120 s while the panel is collapsed and the window is visible, including while away. It is a single setTimeout chain, with no rAF.
   - Extra checks on 'kt:show', 'unlock-screen' and 'resume'. The 20 s poll while open stays.
   - New module src/libs/utils/ui/attention.ts compares question ids against a local seen set (storage key 'kt-desktop.attention.v1': seen{id: firstSeenMs}, announced{id: ms}, reminded{id: ms}, snoozedUntil{id: ms}, lastArrivalMs, lastGreetingDay, lastCaughtUpDay; pruned after 7 days).
   - hasQuestion becomes attention.glyphVisible(): a pending question exists that is not snoozed, whether or not the panel is open.
2. Each question gets exactly one arrival, timed to when someone is there:
   - The arrival animation plays at most once per question id, ever.
   - At least 20 min between arrival animations. A second question inside that window is silent (glyph and badge only). In practice the server already allows at most 3 per day and 1 open, with a 30 min cooldown (defaultCoordinatorSettings), so this rarely triggers.
   - No arrival animation while the person is not at the machine. When a new question is detected, the renderer asks main through 'kt:presence'. If powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime() >= 120 s, the arrival is deferred, and main polls idle time every 10 s, only while something is deferred, until it falls below 3 s. The hop then plays when they are back.
   - The rule: never animate to an empty room, and from across the room the one movement you see is a real event.
   - Presence uses only coarse system idle seconds, never which apps are in use. It is behind a flag because the lab brief warns against implying desktop awareness (open question).
3. Being ignored gracefully:
   - No re-announcement and no escalation.
   - At most one reminder per question: a single 'peek' on a later return to the desk.
   - The glyph stays still and quiet until the question is answered, withdrawn or expires on the server. It then disappears quietly with no act.
   - No sad expression is ever tied to waiting.
   - Later snoozes the glyph for that id for 3 h. After that the glyph returns without any act.
   - Dismiss removes it for good.
4. Answering is short and acknowledged:
   - Click the glyph-bearing Snowbally (opens on the question, Yes focused), then answer. Two clicks.
   - Yes and No get the same hello. Not sure, Later and Dismiss get a friendly nod. The receipt keeps the existing words about what the answer did, plus Undo.
   - Proposed flag autoCloseAfterAnswer, default on: when the panel was opened from the glyph or the peek, it collapses 5 s after the receipt, cancelled while the pointer is over the card or focus is inside it. Clicking Snowbally within 30 s reopens the receipt with Undo, so Undo is never lost.
   - If he came out of hiding to ask, he goes back afterwards.
5. A reason to come back:
   - The welcome-back greeting (stretching on the first return of the day; hello after more than 2 h).
   - The once-a-day backflip when you have answered everything he had.
   - He remembers where you put him.
   - These are rewards for presence, not demands for it.
6. Fidgets, changed from the brief:
   - Not every 45 to 90 s. That would be about 50 peripheral motions an hour, and peripheral motion is the strongest attention grab there is.
   - First fidget only after at least 10 min with no interaction with Snowbally or the panel. Then a random interval of 8 to 15 min, at most 3 per hour.
   - Only 'stretching' and 'peek'.
   - Never while a glyph is showing (motion next to a pending question would read as nagging), never while the panel is open, away, dragging, under reduced motion or hidden.
   - Flag "Little idle moves" (Settings row and context menu, default on).

WHAT IS SEEN FROM ACROSS THE ROOM: honestly, very little.
- One 16 px hop, only when there is a question and someone is present.
- The landing plop when he is moved.
- Otherwise the existing three-pose breathing (1 px).
The 10 x 14 CSS px glyph and the tray '?' are for when you are back at your desk. That is intended: stillness means "nothing for you".

MEASURE LOCALLY ONLY:
- Storage key 'kt-desktop.engagement.v1', per local ISO day, 30 days kept.
- Counters: arrived, arrivalAnimated, arrivalDeferredForPresence, openedFromGlyph, openedFromPeek, openedOther, answered{yes, no, unknown}, later, dismissed, laterThenAnswered, remindersPlayed, ignored24h, undo, autoClosed, awaySessions plus total away minutes, returnsBy{tab, tray, shortcut, peekClick, relaunch}, drags, fidgetsPlayed, clicksWithin60sOfFidget.
- Derived in status(): median time from arrival to opening; open rate within 1 h; dismiss share; discoverability of each return path; minutes away per day (a proxy for "he is in the way").
- Exposed through panel.status().engagement for the harness, plus a "Clear local stats" button in Settings.
- Nothing is sent anywhere, and there are no model calls. Following the lab brief, answer counts alone are not treated as success. These are signals to discuss with Artem, not targets.
proposals.performance:
IDLE (must stay ≤ 0.3 % CPU with no rAF):
- Unchanged idle3 path: three poses held for 500 ms with setTimeout (AvatarController.rest), about 2 draws per second, no rAF.
- The glyph overlay and the cursor-gaze variant reuse the same timer; gaze changes add one draw per change.
- While away, the display canvas is off-window, so the existing IntersectionObserver stops the idle timer. The tab canvas is static, so zero timers are running.
- The background question check is one setTimeout every 120 s plus a local HTTP GET.
- The fidget scheduler is one pending setTimeout.
- Presence polling (10 s) exists only while an arrival is deferred.
- The harness idle CPU window grows from 3 s to 10 s and reports whether a poll happened inside it.

INTERACTION:
- Per pointermove during a drag: one transform write (dock translate3d for x, .rf-drop translateY for y). No layout, because nothing changes left/top/width.
- Pose redraws only when the pose key changes, about 2 to 6 per drag.
- Fall: rAF for its duration with a per-frame transform, and a redraw only on streak changes (16 per second, as R28).
- Roll: rAF for 0.3 to 0.9 s, redraw only on turn changes (16 per second).
- Landing acts: the existing run() loop.
- Opening the panel at a new place: one data-side attribute write, then the frozen springs. Open and close frames must stay ≤ 20 ms; today they measure about 9 ms at 120 Hz.

FULL-WORK-AREA WINDOW COST:
- Forwarded mousemove now arrives whenever the cursor is anything over the work area, so the handler is made O(1) with cached-rect arithmetic instead of elementFromPoint and returns early beyond 200 px.
- The backing store grows with window area. Roughly 3024 x 1898 x 4 B ≈ 23 MB at 2x on a 14-inch screen, versus about 6 MB for the 420 px column. Chromium only rasterises tiles with content, and transparent regions are not repainted.

HARNESS ADDITIONS (shots.ts):
1. idleCpu over 10 s collapsed, plus the same while away (expected lower).
2. mousemoveCpu: 3 s of webContents.sendInputEvent mouseMove at 60 Hz far from Snowbally; renderer ≤ 1.0 %, total ≤ 1.5 %.
3. GPU/renderer memory from app.getAppMetrics() for full-area versus KT_WINDOW_MODE=column: delta ≤ 40 MB.
4. WindowServer CPU sampled with `ps -o %cpu -p $(pgrep WindowServer)` across idle 10 s: no regression greater than 0.5 % against column mode.
5. dragFrames, fallFrames, leaveFrames and returnFrames with frameStats (max ≤ 20 ms, over20ms = 0).
6. Pose latency: the time from the synthetic mouseDown to the next frame shows the PRESS draw (lastFrame or mode change) within 1 frame.
7. The hitbox check is now measured relative to the dock: positions differ by design after a drag, but the bottom must equal floorY and the size must stay 64 x 64.
8. Arrival tests with a mock clock: hop plays once per id, is deferred while presence is idle, plays the peek-in while away, and never animates under reduced motion.
9. Zero console errors.
risks: Full-work-area click-through window: if the ignore state goes stale (a missed mouseleave, an IPC race), clicks meant for other apps could be swallowed anywhere on screen. Today this could only happen within 420 px. Mitigation: pin setIgnore(false) only during drags, force true on blur, mouseleave and drag end, and add a harness check that the window ignores events after every scenario. The KT_WINDOW_MODE=column fallback exists.

Mirrored panel (data-side=left) is a layout variant of a frozen design. Even though no value changes, Artem may see it as a departure; the alternative (nudging him right before opening) moves him from where he was put.

Presence-deferred arrivals use powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime(). That is coarse and app-agnostic, but the lab brief cautions against implying desktop awareness. Keep it behind a flag and in DECISIONS.md.
Fewer animations means a question can go unnoticed (one hop, a small glyph). That trade-off is deliberate, but it should be checked against the local time-to-open metric before adding any escalation.
Background polling while collapsed adds a GET every 120 s. It stays local, but the idle CPU harness must account for it, or the 0.3 % check becomes flaky.
Global shortcut collisions (network engineers live in terminals). Registration failure has to be graceful, and the key choice is open.
Trackpad tap jitter or a slow press misread as a drag, or the reverse. Mitigated by the 4 px threshold plus the 180 ms / 8 px click allowance, and needs hands-on testing.
Auto-close after an answer could hide Undo. Mitigated by reopening the receipt within 30 s and cancelling while the pointer is on the card.
IntersectionObserver-based pausing while away depends on the canvas being fully outside the window. If any pixel overlaps, the idle timer keeps running; assert it in the harness.
The quarter view in the kit faces right only (drawFace adds +2), so leftward drags and rolls show front view plus gaze. Acceptable, but slightly asymmetric.

Display changes (Dock auto-hide, resolution switch) resize the window under an open panel. Clamping and the panel's existing resize handler (motion.view(false); settle) should cover it, but this is untested on a real machine with the Dock moved to the left or right.

proposals.title: Snowbally UX pass: the smallest set of mechanisms. A carrier window that moves with him, one IPC drag channel, a presence state machine and a priority-guarded reaction map
proposals.summary: You can now grab Snowbally. As soon as you press on him he crouches (the authored Springy-tap squash frame), so the first frame already answers you. Move 4 px and he is lifted with his feet dangling, eyes on where you are going. Drag him anywhere along the bottom of the screen; let go up high and he falls with the same gravity as the launch drop and lands with the authored plop (a small hop landing for short drops, the full impact-stars-hello for long ones). He stays where you put him after a restart, and the panel always opens next to him: to his left, or mirrored to his right near the left edge of the screen. When he is in the way, drag him past a screen edge (or use the tray or a shortcut). He hops off and leaves a 16 px sliver of his side, cheek showing, at the floor. Click that sliver, or use the tray or the shortcut, and he hops back with the authored "Hello again" beat. If a new question arrives while he is away, he peeks back to the screen edge once, glances with the question glyph, then waits there quietly. Answering gets a warm wave for Yes/No, an attentive glance for Not sure/Later and a quiet settle for Dismiss, with no guilt and no repeat summons. Nothing animates under reduced motion and nothing ever leaves the machine.
proposals.window:
Decision: keep one small transparent window and move the window itself. I call it the carrier window. I reject the brief's full-work-area window, for robustness reasons.

CURRENT (read in window.ts/main.ts/renderer.ts): 420 px wide, height = workArea.height - 12 (windowHeight()), placed bottom-right with a 12 px margin (placeBottomRight), frame:false, transparent, alwaysOnTop 'floating', setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true,{visibleOnFullScreen:true}), start setIgnoreMouseEvents(true,{forward:true}). The renderer flips ignore off whenever elementFromPoint hits '.rf-avatar, .rf-surface' (IPC 'kt:ignore-mouse'). The panel .rf-window is centred in the window (left:50%; translateX(-50%); bottom:44px). The 64 px .rf-avatar sits at right:15px; bottom:-24px.

PROPOSAL (flag CARRIER, src/apps/desktop/flags.ts):
1. Width 720 DIP (CARRIER_W), height unchanged (work-area height, so the R28 fall and in-air drops still work). Snowbally's 64 px hitbox is pinned at window x 328–392 (centre 360 = CARRIER_W/2) in every state, so the harness invariant "hitbox stationary" still holds, in window coordinates. Desktop-only CSS (marked "desktop (R30)"): `#kt-panel.rf-carrier .rf-window{left:calc(50% - 333px);transform:none}` (panel spans centre-333..centre+47, avatar at its bottom-right as frozen) and `.rf-stage[data-side="right"] .rf-window{left:calc(50% - 47px)}` + `[data-side="right"] .rf-avatar{right:auto;left:15px}` (mirror, avatar at the panel's bottom-left; the hitbox is again 328–392). All type, spacing, colours and springs are untouched. In panel-motion.ts, render() takes a `side()` getter and only swaps the clip-path origin, `inset(T 0 0 L)` to `inset(T L 0 0)`, plus skin.left to skin.right. Spring constants are untouched. The side is decided only when the panel opens: 'right' if the avatar centre is < 353 DIP from workArea.x, otherwise 'left'. It never flips while the panel is open. Below 720 (the harness's 420/320 walks) the .rf-carrier class is absent and today's CSS applies unchanged, including the 419 px compact breakpoint.
2. All horizontal motion is window motion (win.setPosition(x, fixedY)); y never changes. Programmatic moves never compensate content offsets inside the window against window moves, so window and canvas cannot tear out of sync. They can at most be ≤1 frame apart in time, which is invisible because the whole picture moves together.
3. Why not full work area: a 1470×~930 pt window is a ~2940×1860 px IOSurface (~22 MB per buffer, 2–3 buffers) against ~11 MB for 720. Forwarded mousemoves would wake the renderer on every pointer move anywhere on the screen, not just in a 720 px strip. Worst of all, any hit-test glitch (renderer hang, Space switch, sleep/wake leaving ignore=false) would make the WHOLE screen unclickable, where today it is one strip.
4. Electron options added: acceptFirstMouse:true (macOS: the first press on the inactive window must reach the page, or the press pose and drag start would need a second click). Main also sets setIgnoreMouseEvents(true,{forward:true}) on 'render-process-gone' and 'unresponsive' so a dead renderer never blocks clicks.
5. Startup placement handshake: the renderer reads localStorage 'kt-companion.v1' {fromRight, away, snoozeDay} and sends 'kt:place'. Main clamps the position, calls setPosition and only then showInactive(). 'ready-to-show' stays as a 1500 ms fallback. Position is stored as the avatar centre's DIP distance from workArea right, so Dock and resolution changes keep him in a sensible place.
6. screen 'display-metrics-changed' / 'display-removed': main recomputes the area, setSize(720, windowHeight()) (rare, so a one-frame resize glitch is accepted), clamps x by fromRight (or re-applies the away tab) and pushes 'kt:geometry'.
7. Off-primary bleed: when a second display sits beside the primary, a partly off-screen window would draw there. While dragging, away or peeking, the renderer sets `clip-path: inset(0 Rpx 0 Lpx)` on #kt-panel computed from geometry (the work-area edge in window coordinates). This is a one-line style write and costs nothing at idle.
8. IPC (preload exposes only these): renderer→main 'kt:drag' ('start'|'move'|'end'), 'kt:move' {x} (programmatic glides), 'kt:place', 'kt:presence' {away, pending}. Main→renderer 'kt:geometry' {area, winX, winW}, 'kt:command' ('away'|'back'|'toggle'), plus the existing 'kt:show'/'kt:ignore-mouse'. Main clamps every x so the avatar centre stays within [area.x-32, area.right+32] at most, rounds to integer DIP, and does nothing else.

macOS pitfalls addressed: transparent always-on-top moves are plain NSWindow frame moves, with no repaint and no resize. Horizontal off-screen positions are allowed for borderless windows (enableLargerThanScreen is a fallback only if a spike shows clamping). setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces with visibleOnFullScreen may turn the process into a UIElement (no Dock icon), so no return path depends on the Dock. Hot corners and Mission Control can start mid-drag: 'lostpointercapture'/'pointercancel'/window 'blur' end the drag as a release at the last position. Focus stealing: a press activates the app (today's click does too). A spike with BrowserWindow type:'panel' (non-activating NSPanel) is listed as an open question rather than shipped. DPR: setPosition works in DIP, so no DPR maths in main. The integer device scale in AvatarController is untouched, and in-window translateY values are rounded to whole device pixels (Math.round(y*dpr)/dpr).
proposals.drag:
Gesture (renderer, new code in src/apps/desktop/drag.ts, wired in renderer.ts; panel.ts exposes onAvatarPointer hooks):
- pointerdown on .rf-avatar (button 0): setPointerCapture(pointerId), remember clientX/Y and t0, then synchronously call avatar.pose('press'). That pose is the authored 'click' frame 1 (crouch, happy), drawn within the event, so it shows on the next frame. The existing motion.press(true) 2 px spring stays. The renderer's hit-test is frozen at ignore=false while a pointer is down.
- Threshold: Euclidean move ≥ 4 CSS px from the down point (window not yet moving, so client coordinates are exact). Below the threshold, pointerup is a click: the existing 'avatar' action (toggle panel), with the tap started at click frame 2 (deep, spring, rebound, settle; 8 frames at 15 fps = 533 ms) so it continues from the press pose instead of popping back to neutral. A long press with no movement is still a click. There is no double-click gesture: it would toggle the panel open and shut, and delaying the first click to detect it costs responsiveness (the brief's double-click backflip is rejected).
- Drag start (threshold crossed): suppressClick=true (a capture-phase 'click' listener eats the click Chromium fires because the hitbox never moved in window coordinates; without it every drag would also toggle the panel). motion.press(false). If the panel is open it is closed quietly (closePanel(), state kept, so one click restores view, draft and context), because the panel must not ride along to a place where it no longer fits. Send 'kt:drag start'; main records grabOffset = getCursorScreenPoint().x - winX.
- Each pointermove (Chromium already coalesces these to one per frame): send 'kt:drag move'. Main reads screen.getCursorScreenPoint() itself (not the renderer's screenX, whose window origin is stale while the window moves, the classic custom-drag jitter) and calls setPosition(clamp(cursor.x - grabOffset), fixedY). Vertical lift is in-window: lift = clamp(downClientY - clientY, 0, dropTop), applied as translateY on the existing .rf-drop canvas (pointer-events:none). The hitbox stays on the floor.
- Carried pose (src/libs/utils/motion/poses.ts, kit parameters only): orb({bottom:80, shape:'stretch', expression: first 120 ms 'surprised' then 'happy', gaze: sign of horizontal velocity with a 2 px/frame deadband (−1/0/1), view: gaze>0 ? 'quarter' : 'front', feet:[{side:-1,lift:-1},{side:1,lift:-1}]}). The negative lift draws the 3×2 contact nubs one row under the body, which reads as dangling. These are existing nubs, not new anatomy. It is drawn on the drop surface. The floor shadow stays on the display canvas via renderFloorShadow, with kit.shadow width 26 while lift < 40 px and 20 above. The canvas is redrawn only when gaze, face or shadow bucket changes (≈2–6 draws per drag), never per move.
- Release ('kt:drag end' via invoke; main replies {winX, area, centerX}):
  - Centre beyond a screen edge (centerX < area.x or > area.right): Leave toward that edge (see leaveReturn).
  - Partly clipped but centre on-screen: snap back so the body is fully visible (window glide 180 ms ease-out), then land.
  - Landing: lift < 6 px: rest() immediately. 6 ≤ lift < 120 px: fall, then 'hop' frames 11–17 (deep, crouch, settle, happy; 437 ms). lift ≥ 120 px: fall, then 'entrance' frames 5–23 (Impact, spring back, dazed stars, "Oh, hello"; 1.19 s), which is R28's landing reused unchanged.
  - Fall: a generalisation of playEntranceThenRest, avatar.fallFrom(dropY, landing). y = start·(1−p²) as R28, with duration T = ENTRANCE_FALL_MS·sqrt(h/D0), where D0 = |fallStart()|. That keeps the same acceleration as the launch: about 330 ms from 120 px on a ~900 px window. The streaks come from renderFalling.
  - Persist fromRight to localStorage 'kt-companion.v1'.
- Edge cases: lostpointercapture, pointercancel, window blur, Mission Control or hot-corner activation, and Space switch all count as a release at the last known position. The cursor above the window (menu bar) clamps lift to the window top. The cursor below the window (Dock) gives lift 0. A drag starting mid-fall is ignored (the hitbox is on the floor during a fall, by design). Reduced motion: the drag still works (direct manipulation, not animation) and the carried pose is a still, but release puts him on the floor instantly with no fall or landing act. Keyboard and accessibility: no drag. Tray 'Reset position' and the away/back commands cover it.

New AvatarController API (avatar.ts, additive): pose(name), play(key,{from,to,loop}), carry(liftPx, dir), fallFrom(dropY, 'hop'|'entrance'), look(dir), and status().lastPoseAt (performance.now() of the last draw, for the latency check).
proposals.leaveReturn:
State machine (src/apps/desktop/presence.ts, renderer side; owns persistence and glides; main only clamps and sets positions): home → dragging → falling → home | leaving → away → peeking → perched | returning → home.

LEAVE: triggered by dragging past an edge, by the tray item "Send Snowbally away", or by the global shortcut (toggle). If the panel is open it closes first (quiet). If he is not at an edge (tray or shortcut from mid-screen), he glides to the nearest edge first at up to 1.6 px/ms, ease-in, capped at 600 ms, holding a still that looks toward the edge (gaze ±1, quarter view when the edge is to his right). Then the exit runs: 'hop' frames 2–9 (dip, stretch, airborne happy; 437 ms at 16 fps), and the window glides out with ease-in (x = start + d·p²) starting at frame 4, so the take-off coincides with motion. Glides are rAF in the renderer sending 'kt:move' each frame, and only for their duration. End state 'away': the window is placed so the 16 CSS px of his body nearest the screen (8 source pixels: contour, white and a cheek pixel) plus 4 px of hitbox margin remain on-screen at the floor, i.e. a 20×64 clickable strip against the screen edge. The edge makes that target infinitely deep for the pointer. The idle loop stops (one still frame and no timers, which is cheaper than idle). The away side is persisted. 'kt:presence' tells main to relabel the tray.

WHAT REMAINS VISIBLE: only that sliver of Snowbally himself, with no new tab art. A brief "tiny pixel tab" is exactly this. Hovering it gives an affordance: the window glides 8 px further out in 120 ms (he leans in), with cursor:pointer, and back on leave. The hover pose is the attentive still.

RETURN (any of):
(a) Click the sliver. This is the discoverable path: it is literally him.
(b) Drag the sliver out, using the same drag code. Releasing on-screen means he is back.
(c) Tray: the left click and the first menu item become "Bring Snowbally back" / "Send Snowbally away" (replacing Show/Hide; the tray stays the place to quit).
(d) Global shortcut, default Control+Command+S (open question), toggling away and back. globalShortcut.register failure is logged and skipped.
(e) The app's 'second-instance' (relaunching the app) also returns him.
(f) Dock 'activate' returns him when a Dock icon exists, but nothing depends on it (see risks).

Return animation: the window glides in from the sliver to the stored home x with ease-out over 437 ms while 'hop' plays frames 4–11 (airborne to Land), then frames 11–17 including the authored beat 14 "Hello again". Total ≈ 0.9 s, after which he rests. If a question is pending and he was returned by clicking the sliver, the question view opens on landing, quietly (programmatic open, per v009). Reduced motion: every glide is an instant setPosition and he appears as a still.

QUESTION WHILE AWAY: the collapsed poll (see engagement) finds a new unseen question. He peeks: the window glides from the sliver to the 'perch' (the whole 88 px canvas visible, 4 px from the edge, so body and glyph both show) with ease-out over 437 ms, plus hop frames 4–11, then the authored 'question' state act (glance plus glyph, 16 frames at 12 fps = 1.33 s), then a still with the glyph. He stays perched with no further motion. Clicking him opens the question; the panel side follows the edge rule. When that interaction ends (panel closed after an answer, or 60 s after the receipt) he hops back to the sliver, because the person put him away and that choice is honoured. If the person sends him away again from the perch without opening the question, peeks are snoozed for the rest of the day (snoozeDay in kt-companion.v1). The tray title shows the pending count meanwhile (tray.setTitle('1'), macOS text beside the icon, no new art), so the question still reaches them. Max peeks per day ≤ the service's daily per-person question limit (3).

LAUNCH: if away was saved he starts at the sliver without the fall, respecting the choice (open question: alternatively always fall in at launch). Otherwise the R28 fall plays at the remembered x.
proposals.reactions:
Single entry point: src/libs/utils/ui/reactions.ts, react(event). Priorities:
- P0 direct manipulation (press, drag, release, landing) interrupts everything.
- P1 acknowledgement of the person's action (tap, answers, input, return) interrupts P2/P3.
- P2 system state (question arrival, result, error, processing loop) does not cut a running P1. It is queued (latest wins) and starts when the P1 act ends.
- P3 ambient (gaze, fidgets) never interrupts. It is dropped if anything is playing, the panel is open, he is away or carried, the document is hidden, or reduced motion is on.
Today AvatarController.play() always stop()s and interrupts; the guard lives in reactions.ts so the controller stays dumb.

Map:
- pointerdown → pose 'press' = click frame 1 (crouch, happy), still, P0, ≤1 frame.
- click (no drag) → toggle panel + play('click',{from:2}), 533 ms, P1 (keeps R29's "tap on every direct click").
- hover enter (panel closed, idle) → 'attentive' still: orb({shape:'high', gaze:±1 toward pointer, view: gaze>0?'quarter':'front'}); the idle timer pauses. Hover leave → rest(). P3 but one draw only. The brief's hover = peek is changed to a still: a 1 s act on every pass of the cursor is jittery and nags.
- cursor within 160 px of his centre (forwarded mousemove already arrives for the hit-test) → look(dir) still with gaze −1/0/1 (|dx| > 24 px deadband, 250 ms hysteresis), drawn only when the bucket changes. Idle cycling pauses while watched and resumes on exit. P3, off in reduced motion.
- drag start → carried pose (see drag). Release → fall + 'hop' 11–17 or 'entrance' 5–23. P0.
- question arrives, present → play('question') (authored glance + glyph, 1.33 s), then idle with the glyph overlay held (P2). The brief's hop is rejected: the lab says "one small pose change, then a static available cue".
- question arrives, away → peek (glide + hop 4–11 + 'question'), once per question.
- open question from the queue → existing play('question').
- Yes / No → play('hello') (0.67 s), the same warm beat for both (lab: correction is as welcome as confirmation). Today respond() plays 'result' for every value.
- Not sure / Later → play('peek') (1.0 s attentive glance, "available"). Dismiss → no act, rest (an easy exit). The brief's 'stretching' (a yawn reads as boredom) and 'half' (sheepish reads as guilt) are rejected, per the lab rule "no disappointment".
- Points awarded (opt-in setting) → play('hop') instead of hello, with the existing burst.
- Last open question of the day answered (queue cleared) → play('backflip') at most once per day (flag, open question).
- Undo → existing setView('question'), plus play('peek').
- Submit → existing processing loop, then 'result'. Typing or attachment → existing 'input'. Errors → existing 'error'. Retry OK → existing 'hello'.
- Leave → look-to-edge still + hop 2–9. Return → hop 4–17 ("Hello again").
- Screen unlock after ≥ 30 min (powerMonitor 'unlock-screen'/'resume', OS events about this machine only) → play('hello') once if he is present, plus a question refresh.
- Idle fidgets (flag FIDGETS) → one of 'stretching' / 'peek' on a single setTimeout of random 4–8 min, at most 6 per hour. Skipped under the P3 rules and whenever the pointer was within 160 px in the last 2 min. The brief's 45–90 s is rejected: it means 40–80 movements an hour in peripheral vision on an always-on-top window. 'hop' is excluded because vertical motion pulls the eye.

Reduced motion (system or setting): every act resolves to its still, as AvatarController already does via canAnimate(). Press, carried, attentive and glyph stills remain because they are state, not motion. No falls, glides, fidgets or gaze tracking. No sound anywhere.
proposals.engagement:
What makes people answer:
(1) Questions reach them without nagging. Today panel.ts polls only while the panel is open (syncPoll: "no timer at all while collapsed"), and hasQuestion() is true only when the question view is open. So a question that arrives while he is collapsed is invisible until the person opens the panel. Fix: a collapsed poll, one setTimeout chain of 60 s (COLLAPSED_POLL_MS), skipped while document.hidden. It also runs immediately on 'kt:show', on unlock/resume and on return. It fetches GET /questions from the local service only. hasQuestion() becomes `panelOpen ? view==='question' : pendingUnseen`, so the authored glyph sits on the idle body whenever an unseen question waits. That is the "static available cue".
(2) Arrival is acknowledged once: one 'question' glance, or one peek while away, then stillness.
(3) One click reaches the question: clicking him while the glyph shows opens straight into the question view (programmatic open, quiet).
(4) Answering is acknowledged warmly and equally: hello for Yes/No, peek for Not sure/Later, quiet for Dismiss, plus the existing receipt and Undo, plus the opt-in points hop and burst.
(5) Coming back is acknowledged: a hello on unlock after ≥ 30 min, the "Hello again" beat whenever he is returned, and a perch that waits for you.
(6) He feels alive under your hand: press, carry, drop and gaze all answer within a frame. That is what makes people want to poke him, and poking him is the path to the panel.

Anti-nag rules: no repeated summons for the same question; at most one peek per question; peeks snoozed for the day if the person sends him away from a perch; no acrobatics for overdue questions; fidgets every 4–8 min at most, never while watched or open; he never returns from away on his own except the bounded peek; no sound.

Local measurement (localStorage 'kt-companion.metrics.v1', exposed in panel.status() for the harness, never sent anywhere): glyphShown, peeks, peekSnoozes, median ms from glyph to question open, answers by kind (yes/no/unknown/later/dismiss), undos, panel opens (direct vs via glyph), drags, leaves and returns by path (sliver/drag/tray/shortcut/peek), fidgets played. Per the lab brief, these are only diagnostic; answer quality and voluntary contributions are the real measure.
